channel.title: NOSE NOTES
channel.description: A San Jose journal of aroma, appetite, and very specific taste.

item.title: Mythbusting: All San Jose Weed Is the Same
item.description: A capped city market does not equal identical flower. Cultivation methods, freshness, testing, and storage still create real differences shoppers can learn to see.

item.title: Rainy Season and Harvest Supply: Why Menus Shift in Fall
item.description: Autumn weather and harvest cycles change what licensed shelves emphasize. Shoppers who understand seasonality stop blaming their favorite counter for every missing SKU.

item.title: Cannabis vs. Cigarettes: National Numbers, Local Stigma at the Counter
item.description: Federal survey tallies and a Gallup poll show a cultural pass for cannabis as cigarettes sit near historic lows. Prevalence is not a medical free pass.

item.title: UGA Study: Legal Medical Cannabis and Sick Days, Limits Included
item.description: University of Georgia researchers linked medical cannabis law timing to fewer health-related absences. Recreational laws did not show the same effect, and the paper is not a doctor’s note.

item.title: Clones and Home-Grow Adjacent Questions, Without the Out-of-Town Promo Travelogue
item.description: Clone shopping raises practical questions for South Bay adults already allowed six plants at home. Stay local, lawful, and neighbor-aware, no road-trip advertisement required.

item.title: Pregnancy, Nursing, and Why Shops Refuse Certain Sales Conversations
item.description: California consumer guidance is blunt: if you are pregnant, may be pregnant, or breastfeeding, do not consume cannabis, and talk to a doctor. Retail staff are not your obstetric team.

item.title: Cannabis and Prescription Meds: Ask a Clinician, Not a Stranger Online
item.description: Budtenders can explain product formats. They cannot reconcile your SSRI, blood thinner, or sleep aid with a new edible. South Bay shoppers need a brighter line.

item.title: Budtenders as Guides: Ten Questions Worth Asking
item.description: In a scarce market with overlapping menus, good questions turn cashiers into guides, without turning them into doctors.

item.title: Cannabis and Coffee: South Bay Cafe-Adjacent Rituals (No Public Use)
item.description: Espresso culture and cannabis culture share mornings, and must not share sidewalks. Pairing is a private ritual under San Jose rules.

item.title: Microdosing Culture in Tech-Heavy San Jose
item.description: Low-dose talk thrives where calendars are dense. Milligrams and honesty beat Silicon Valley mythmaking about productivity chemicals.

item.title: Tolerance Breaks: How Locals Actually Talk About Resets
item.description: T-breaks are ordinary adult maintenance in a mature market, not a moral purge. Planning beats white-knuckle improvisation.

item.title: Topicals and Bath Products: What They Can and Can’t Do
item.description: Balms, lotions, and bath soaks occupy the wellness endcap. Localized application is the usual frame, intoxication and miracle claims are not.

item.title: Concentrates Ladder: Cure Resin to Live Rosin Without Snobbery
item.description: From budget distillate to solventless rosin, potency climbs and prices follow. A ladder helps shoppers climb on purpose, not for status.

item.title: Vape Hardware Safety: Batteries, Counterfeits, Legal Carts Only
item.description: Legal carts and working batteries beat mystery hardware. Counterfeits and abused cells turn a discreet format into a hazard.

item.title: Fall Terpene Guide: Pine, Citrus, Berry, Shopping by Nose
item.description: Seasonal shopping language, woodsy pine, bright citrus, dessert berry, helps budtender chats without pretending THC percent equals flavor.

item.title: Pre-Roll Quality Tells: Canoeing, Shake, Infused vs. Classic
item.description: Machine-rolled convenience meets uneven burns and mystery trim. A few quality tells help San Jose shoppers spend on purpose.

item.title: Indica/Sativa Folk Labels vs. Modern Hybrid Reality
item.description: “Indica sleepy, sativa racy” still shapes menus. Modern genetics and chemistry tell a messier story, read cannabinoids and terpenes, not just the folk tag.

item.title: Heat Waves and Storage: Keeping Flower Fresh in a South Bay Summer
item.description: Hot cars and sunny windowsills punish terpenes and cannabinoids. Cool, dark, airtight storage is the unglamorous half of a good eighth.

item.title: Air-Quality and Wildfire Smoke Days: Lung-Conscious Alternatives
item.description: When the hills haze over, adding cannabis smoke is a choice. CDC wildfire and lung guidance points shoppers toward cleaner indoor air and non-inhaled options.

item.title: UCSF Cannabis Heart-Rhythm Study, Caveats for Wellness Readers
item.description: A Bay Area trial found fewer premature heartbeats on inhalation days among habitual users. UCSF scientists said not to treat the result as medical advice, and shoppers should echo that hedge.

item.title: Exercise and Cannabis: Local Gym-Culture Questions
item.description: South Bay fitness talk meets legal cannabis at the edges, timing, lung load, and workplace rules, not at a mythical performance shortcut.

item.title: Sleep Products: What Labels Claim vs. What Evidence Says
item.description: CBN-forward gummies and “nighttime” ratios pack shelves. Human sleep evidence is thinner than the packaging, and San Jose shoppers deserve the hedges.

item.title: High-CBD and Balanced Ratios for Anxious Shoppers
item.description: Ratio products are a shopping language, not a diagnosis. Evidence on CBD and anxiety is promising in places and limited overall, hedge the hype at the counter.

item.title: Cannabis Beverages and Nano-Emulsions: Why a Drink Can Hit Differently
item.description: Emulsified drinks promise faster onset than classic baked edibles. Pharmacokinetic studies support faster absorption for some nanoformulations, without turning cans into soft drinks.

item.title: Edibles Onset and Dosing for Bay Area First-Timers
item.description: Delayed effects, milligram labels, and patience beat folklore. San Jose’s licensed shelves reward adults who start low and wait.

item.title: Seniors Shopping Cannabis in San Jose: Pacing, Edibles, Questions
item.description: Start low, go slow, read milligrams, and bring a clinician into the conversation when medications are involved.

item.title: Pesticides, Mold, and What Cannabis Testing Is Supposed to Catch
item.description: Lab panels are a safety net, not a flavor guarantee, and illicit product skips the net entirely.

item.title: Track-and-Trace and Lab Testing: Why the Sticker Matters
item.description: METRC-era tracking and mandatory testing are the quiet infrastructure behind every legal San Jose jar.

item.title: How to Read a California Cannabis Label (THC, Terpenes, Batch)
item.description: The sticker is the product’s résumé, THC, CBD, batch ID, and warnings beat the strain nickname on the shelf talker.

item.title: First-Timer Glossary: Flower, Preroll, Cart, Rosin, RSO
item.description: A plain-language map of the shelf so a first San Jose counter visit is less overwhelming.
